gloss: to look down on; to make light of

definitions.gloss: to look down on; to make light of; to belittle
definitions.explanation: To treat something or someone as unimportant or insignificant. Often used in formal or written contexts to describe disrespect or undervaluation.

examples.japanese: {命|いのち}を{軽|かろ}んじてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not make light of life.

examples.japanese: {伝統|でんとう}を{軽|かろ}んじる{態度|たいど}は{問題|もんだい}だ。
examples.english: An attitude that belittles tradition is problematic.

examples.japanese: {他人|たにん}の{意見|いけん}を{軽|かろ}んじると、{信頼|しんらい}を{失|うしな}うことになる。
examples.english: If you belittle other people's opinions, you'll end up losing their trust.

notes:
USAGE:
{軽|かろ}んじる is a literary and formal verb. In everyday speech, {軽|かる}く{見|み}る or ばかにする are more common. It appears frequently in written commentary, editorials, and formal discourse.

GRAMMAR:
Kami-ichidan (ru-verb). Transitive. The older form {軽|かろ}んずる also exists but is archaic.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {命|いのち}を{軽|かろ}んじる (to make light of life)
- {人権|じんけん}を{軽|かろ}んじる (to disregard human rights)
- {伝統|でんとう}を{軽|かろ}んじる (to belittle tradition)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {侮|あなど}る: to look down on, to scorn
- {見下|みくだ}す: to look down on (more colloquial)
- {蔑|さげす}む: to despise, to hold in contempt
